newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil consolidates on recovery.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil consolidates on recovery.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps sustained last week's recovery by midday Monday on technical buying and on the back of a rise in crude and heating oil prices on NYMEX ACCESS after-hours trading, traders said.
"Gas oil continued its rebound with a U.S. trader seen as the main buyer while a Chinese trader is the main seller," one trader said.
"The market is consolidating but the (physical) fundamentals remained weak," he said, referring to the high stocks in the region which was not being met with sufficient demand.
Another broker said there were three active players in the market.
July paper was last quoted at $22.25/$22.45 per barrel, up from late Friday's $22.20/$22.35, brokers said. July traded this morning at $22.25 and $22.35.
August was last quoted at $22.80/$22.95, up from Friday's $22.70/$22.85.

Brokers said the market is in a steep contango with September being bid at $23.35, signalling some confidence that demand would start picking up from August and September as regional buyers stock up for the cold season.

But despite the current recovery, which some traders believe will not last, the prompt month for physical cargoes were traded at a low level, with a European major buying from a U.S. major at $21.50 on Friday.
The bears in the market also pointed out to the brimming middle-distillate stocks at Mobil Oil Singapore's refinery which they said would maintain prices at low levels.

Traders said unlike gas oil the short term outlook appeared brighter for jet fuel, especially on demand from Indonesia. On Friday the jet/gas oil regrade for July was traded at $1.60 per barrel and was notionally bid for July and August at $1.10 on
Fuel oil swaps was last quoted $1.00 higher from Friday for July at $99/$100 per tonne, amid resurgent buying interest on the physical market. July was heard traded this morning at $99.75.
August also rose to be last indicated at $98.00/$99.50 from Friday's $97.75/$98.50
